lines.trans: What kind of strange help is that?
I know Vitya better than he knows himself.
But you already had an agreement with him.
And then he went and lost everything.
Right now I need him in top form.
Believe me, he will beat all the competitors.
And he will bring us the first star in Russia.
That is what is called a smart strategy.
And this right here is called our bedroom.
And I feel so lonely in it.
Do not play the fool tonight, Dima.
Nothing but great strategists gathered all around.

examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.

examples.text: Что здесь вообще сейчас происходит?
examples.trans: What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('great').

examples.text: Кругом одни великие стратеги собрались.
examples.trans: Nothing but great strategists gathered all around.

examples.text: Великий хан.
examples.trans: The great Khan.

examples.text: Великий русский писатель.
examples.trans: A great Russian writer.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тратег'). Common masculine noun meaning 'strategists' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вот это и называется умная стратегия.
examples.trans: That is what is called a smart strategy.

examples.text: Кругом одни великие стратеги собрались.
examples.trans: Nothing but great strategists gathered all around.

meanings.en: to intend, plan, get ready to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'gathered', paired with 'собираться'.

examples.text: Ты что, уходить от меня собрался?
examples.trans: Are you planning to leave me or what?

examples.text: Мы собрались в отпуск.
examples.trans: We got ready for vacation.

examples.text: Вы что, пить алкоголь собрались?
examples.trans: Are you planning to drink alcohol?

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.text: Ты же всегда мечтала писать книги.
examples.trans: You have always dreamed of writing books.

examples.text: Один я всегда на передовой.
examples.trans: Only I am always on the front line.

examples.text: У неё всегда так.
examples.trans: She's always like that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Там про меня всё написано в интернете.
examples.trans: Everything about me is written on the internet.

examples.text: Михаилу Джековичу сейчас нужна помощь.
examples.trans: Mikhail Dzhekovich needs help right now.

examples.text: Ничего, что это наша раковина?
examples.trans: Do you mind that this is our sink?

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'довая'). Common feminine noun meaning 'front line' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Один я всегда на передовой.
examples.trans: Only I am always on the front line.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть передовая.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always front line.
